ut_campsite_7.blurb: Campsite 7 is a small crag up Green Canyon in Cache Valley, above Logan, in the northern Wasatch. It mixes about seven sport lines, mostly 5.10 with one 5.9 and a couple of 5.11s, with ten boulder problems that run from V2 up to the V10-V11 range. The climbs are short, roughly 20 to 40 feet, with bouldery moves, so it suits newer leaders as well as people chasing harder problems. Most of the lines sit in the cave right in front of the car spot, and the canyon is usually quiet. Descent is by lowering or rappelling off the chains.

ut_cinema_the.blurb: The Cinema is a sandstone sport crag beside the Colorado River on River Road (UT-128) east of Moab, one of several walls at Take-Out Beach. Of its 17 climbs, 16 are bolted, with a single easy crack for trad. The grades are friendly: a few 5.6 and 5.7 starters, a cluster at 5.9, and the bulk at 5.10, with one route reaching 5.11. Reaching the wall means a short trail across from the beach parking, including a bit of third-class scrambling, then a walk past The Theater. Good for a relaxed day of moderate bolted climbing.

ut_cold_war_crags.blurb: Cold War Crags is a cluster of walls at roughly 7,000 feet in the Mill Creek area of the La Sal Mountains near Moab. The sandstone walls offer crack and face climbing, split almost evenly between sport and trad, and the grades start at the 5.10 level and run mostly through 5.11 and 5.12 into the low 5.13s. The walls face north and stay cool, with plenty of shade for much of the day, which makes it a place to escape valley heat. The East Berlin wall is entered by rappelling in and leaving up a fixed line, so it is not a casual stop.

ut_moab_rim_trail_boulders.blurb: These are scattered sandstone boulders along the Moab Rim jeep road above Kane Creek Boulevard near Moab. The best concentration is the Labyrinth, a cluster of well-featured blocks roughly 0.4 miles up the road from the trailhead parking. Most of the 17 problems are easy to moderate, with a lot of V0 to V3 and a handful of harder lines reaching V6 and V7. The climbing includes steep roof starts and inverted features, and a pad or two is all the landings call for. Expect shared use of the road by vehicles and bikes.
ut_moab_rim_trail_boulders.parking_note: Leave the car at the Moab Rim trailhead on Kane Creek Boulevard, then walk up the jeep road.

ut_buoux_area.blurb: The Buoux Area is a quiet, sunny bouldering zone in the Right Fork of Joe's Valley, near Orangeville in central Utah. The sandstone problems are scattered among desert trees a short walk from a large camping and parking area. With 17 problems, the grades centre on V2 to V4, with a handful of V0 and V1 warm-ups and a few harder lines up to about V9. The Bowling Ball and the Buoux boulder lines are among the best known. Rock is porous and weaker when wet, so wait for it to dry fully.

ut_matrix_the.blurb: The Matrix is a wall of sport routes in the Middle Fork of Maple Canyon in central Utah, on the conglomerate cobble rock the canyon is known for. All 17 climbs are bolted, with one 5.8 and the rest split between 5.10 and 5.11 with a few at 5.12. High walls across the drainage keep it shaded for most of the day, so it works well on warm days. The approach follows the well-used footpath west up the Middle Fork for about 8 to 10 minutes from the roadside pullout.

ut_mosquito_wall.blurb: Mosquito Wall is a small cliff beside the Mirror Lake Highway in the Uinta Mountains of northeast Utah, with well-bolted moderate lines. Of the 17 routes, 15 are sport and two are trad, running from 5.6 to 5.10, with most in the 5.7 to 5.9 range. The wall goes from slab to vertical with some bulges and small roofs; it is short on the left and taller on the right, around 70 feet. A trail of about ten minutes climbs through the trees from a roadside pullout. The wall is good for a short visit, and bugs can be thick near the end of the day.

ut_big_joe.blurb: Big Joe is a bouldering area in the Left Fork of Joe's Valley, centred on a large sandstone boulder with a steep roof that holds several classic problems; more boulders sit up the gully behind. Parking is at the pullout by the riverside area, and the boulder is about 50 yards up the hill across the road. The 17 problems span a wide range, from V0 slabs through the middle grades to roof lines at V7 and beyond, up to about V11. The area is heavily visited. The rock is porous and weak when wet, so let it dry for days after any rain.

_conflicts.ut_matrix_the: Stored aspect is NW, but https://www.mountainproject.com/area/105836291/the-matrix says left-side routes face southwest and right-side routes face south to southeast; stored value left unchanged.
